deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 3 of Grothendieck's preparatory notes for his Nov.–Dec. 1967 IHES lectures on crystals, 'Revue des essais de définitions d'une théorie cohomologique en car. p>0'. Approach 1) (begun on p.13) uses flat (fppf) cohomology with radicial/infinitesimal group-scheme coefficients (mu_{p^n}, alpha_p, ...) as a candidate p-adic cohomology. This page continues that approach.

(i) Dimension 1. For curves over a field, possibly finite, flat cohomology of radicial coefficients gives a good duality theory: a geometric, flat-cohomology form of class field theory and duality for curves. Grothendieck hopes Raynaud will clarify this theory and its local analogues, which will require overcoming considerable technical obstacles. This was later done by Artin–Milne (global, curves, 1976) and Bégueri (local, 1980), not by Raynaud.

(ii) Dimension n >= 2. The approach is 'sans espoir' as a Weil cohomology. He cites a remark of Artin that the relevant flat cohomology groups (H^i(X, mu_p)-type) vanish, or are trivial in the relevant sense, in degrees > n+1. So flat cohomology with radicial coefficients has range dim X + 1, not 2 dim X, even for X projective and smooth. It therefore cannot have the Betti numbers or the 2n-dimensional Poincaré duality required of a Weil cohomology. One only recovers certain 'good' cohomological invariants by this route, and any duality would have to be a modified ('compliquée') version of Poincaré duality with total degree n+1.

(iii) Conclusion, continued on p.15. One needs a definition of p-adic cohomology independent of choices, relating only indirectly to flat cohomology. This motivates the passage to Washnitzer–Monsky and to de Rham/crystalline cohomology.

Modern reading: H^i_fl(X, mu_{p^n}) is about H^{i-1}(X, W_n Omega^1_log). Flat/logarithmic de Rham–Witt cohomology of the various Z/p^n(r) has cohomological range d+1. Milne's duality (1976 for surfaces, 1986 in general) pairs Z/p^n(r) with Z/p^n(d-r) with shift d+1, exactly the 'dim X + 1, not 2 dim X' phenomenon noted here.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The statement of Artin's remark is too illegible to verify precisely. The correct fact is that fppf cohomology of mu_{p^n} on a smooth proper n-dimensional variety over an algebraically closed field vanishes above degree n+1 (in fact above n for the coherent-type parts). Read as a vanishing/cd bound, the claim is correct.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a historical survey of known approaches, and its content is essentially in the published 1968 crystals lecture notes. The flat-duality expectations were later realized by Artin–Milne, Bégueri and Milne. The small points of interest are the expectation that Raynaud would develop flat duality, and the clear early statement that flat duality has total degree dim X + 1, anticipating Milne's duality. Neither amounts to a missed result.
transcription_corrections: Line 3–5: 'et ses analogues locales — ce qui exigera d'ailleurs de surmonter des obstacles techniques considérables' ('des' is struck, replaced by an overwritten word before 'obstacles').
'il est sans espoir' is probably 'il est sans espoir' / 'sans emploi'. 'car Artin a remarqué que tous les' is followed by a phrase with a struck-out underlined portion under 'de dim. en X'.
'(et non 2 dim X, quand X est somme)': 'somme' is likely 'lisse' (or 'propre').

Near the bottom, the inserted phrase above '(compliquer la' is probably 'n-2 mais'. The following lines read roughly 'dualité de ... tableau par heuristiques par Poincaré....' rather than 'dualité de Lefschetz'.
'Donc on cherche les classes' may instead read 'Donc on obtient seulement les classes...', referring to obtaining only certain combinations of 'bons' invariants cohomologiques par cette voie.
